limitations: The overall quality of the included studies remains as 'fair' according to the protocol of the National Institutes of Health quality assessment tool, indicating possible biases.
The validation analysis of sample size has not been clearly reported in some studies, which might reduce the generalizability of the achieved findings.

Over half of the reviewed studies adopted cross-sectional surveys to collect subjective evaluation of perceived environmental features via self-reported questionnaires, which are less suitable for providing strong evidence for specific interventions.

Controlled intervention experiments and longitudinal studies in the included studies have mainly explored effects of conventional environmental characteristics, with less attention to other PIEC domains (e.g., decoration, naturalness, perceived privacy).
Articles published in non-English sources and grey literature were not included.
Some studies meeting the inclusion criteria may not have been retrieved due to the search syntax used in this review.
Possible biases occurred in the review process despite individual evaluation by reviewers following a strict protocol.
